title: Egg salad sandwiches
skill: Boiling eggs hard and peeling them

notes.text: Boil the eggs in the large pot so they sit in one layer.

move.title: Hard-boil, chill, peel
move.body: Egg salad starts with hard-boiled eggs. Today you'll cook eggs in hot water, cool them in ice water so they peel easily, and chop them into a creamy salad for sandwiches.

callback.body: Tuna salad sandwiches mixed tuna with mayonnaise and mustard. Egg salad is the same sandwich with chopped hard-boiled eggs instead of tuna.

why.title: Boil, then turn it off
why.body: Eggs cooked at a hard boil turn rubbery. Here the water boils, the heat goes off, and the hot water cooks them gently.

why.title: The ice bath
why.body: Ice water stops the cooking, so there's no gray-green ring around the yolk. It also makes the shell easier to peel.

why.title: Peel from the wide end
why.body: The wide end has a little air pocket. Start there, and the shell comes off in big pieces.

why.title: Keep it cold
why.body: Egg salad has mayonnaise and cooked eggs. Keep it in the fridge, and eat it within 3 days.

wrong.sign: There's a gray-green ring around the yolk
wrong.fix: The eggs cooked too long or cooled too slowly. They're fine to eat.
Peel it under running water. Very fresh eggs are hardest to peel.
Chop one more egg and stir it in.

quiz.q: Why do the eggs go into ice water?
choices: To stop the cooking and help them peel
To make them colder to eat
quiz.explain: No green ring, and easier peeling.

quiz.q: How long does egg salad keep in the fridge?

steps.text: Lower the eggs into the saucepan with the slotted spoon. Add cold water to cover them by 1 inch.
steps.tip: Lower them gently so they don't crack.

steps.text: Bring the water to a boil over high heat, with the lid off.
Turn off the burner. Put the lid on and leave the eggs in the hot water.
Fill the large bowl with cold water and ice.
steps.look: More ice than water is fine.

steps.text: With the slotted spoon, move the eggs into the ice water.
Tap each egg on the counter and roll it. Peel it from the wide end.
steps.look: Smooth white eggs, no bits of shell.
steps.tip: Rinse off any little bits of shell.

steps.text: Cut one egg in half. The yolk should be yellow and firm all the way through.

target.look: Firm yellow yolk, no runny middle

steps.text: Snip the chives into small pieces with the kitchen shears.
Put the eggs in the medium bowl. Chop them up with the side of the fork.
steps.look: Small pieces, about the size of peas.

steps.text: Add the mayonnaise, mustard, chives, salt, and pepper. Stir gently.
steps.look: Creamy, with bits of white and yellow.

steps.text: Taste a little on a clean spoon. Add a pinch of salt if it needs it.
Lay out 4 slices of bread. Add lettuce if you like. Spread on the egg salad.
steps.tip: Spread it right to the edges.

steps.text: Top with the other 4 slices. Cut each sandwich in half with the butter knife.
